summary.en: Militant groups continue to launch lethal attacks against Pakistani security forces, with recent assaults killing ten police officers and 18 fighters in northwest Pakistan and another ambush causing similar casualties. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, police faced a clash that left eleven officers feared dead and a separate incident in Kohat that injured twelve personnel. Efforts to reopen borders for trade are ongoing, while a review of alleged war crimes in Afghanistan noted missing key photographic evidence. The conflict still accounts for 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantgrupper fortsetter å gjennomføre dødelige angrep mot pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker, med nylige angrep som drepte ti politifolk og 18 kampere i nordvestlige Pakistan og et annet bakholdsangrep som forårsaket lignende tap. I Khyber Pakhtunkhwa møtte politiet en sammenstøt som etter sigende etterlot elleve offiserer døde, og en separat hendelse i Kohat så tolv personer bli såret. Arbeidet med å gjenåpne grenser for handel pågår, mens en gjennomgang av påståtte krigsforbrytelser i Afghanistan påpekte at viktig fotografisk bevis mangler. Konflikten står fortsatt for 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
